JUDGMENT

This suit is filed by the plaintiff to declare that the plaintiff No.1 is entitled for suit schedule property by declaring that the registered sale deed dated 10.07.2003 executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No.2 and the gift deed dated 02.03.2025 executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.2(a) is not binding on the plaintiff.
2.
The case of the plaintiffs in brief is as hereunder:-

The defendant No.1 Society allotted a residential site bearing No.341 in the layout formed by defendant No.1 in Sy.No.30 & 31 of Devasandra village measuring 30x40 feet in favour of one late Abdul Hafeez, who is the father of defendant No.2 and executed a registered sale deed dated 15.09.1962 for a consideration amount of 400/-.
Thereafter, original allottee Abdul Hafeez sold the same in favour of the plaintiff No.1 G.Jayaram for a consideration amount of 1,500/- through the registered sale deed dated 29.09.1966.
Later the plaintiff No.1 G.Jayaram has let out it on lease in favour of one Krishna Rao on 18.01.1967 through a registered lease deed and enjoyed it.
Later the CITB did not approve the layout and therefore the entire plan was changed.
Site No.341 allotted earlier was used for civic amenities and widening the road.
Thereafter, the plaintiff has even paid layout charges to the CITB as per the notification dated 19.11.1974.
The plaintiff has requested the defendant No.1 to reallot the alternative Site.
Accordingly, the defendant No.1 had reallotted Site No.102 measuring 30x40 feet.

But, later the plaintiff came to know that the defendant No.1 has allotted alternative Site No.102 to the defendant No.2 on 10.07.2003 for which the plaintiff issued a notice dated 18.06.2004 to defendant No.1.
It is informed by the defendant No.1 that the defendant No.2 has played fraud and obtained the sale deed for which the plaintiff is entitled and therefore instituted this suit.
3. Pursuant to the suit summons issued by this Court, defendants No.1 & 2 entered appearance and filed the written statement.

In the written statement filed by defendant No.1, it has taken up a contention that the defendant No.2 Abdul Rakeeb made false representation, suppressed material facts and fraudulently obtained the registered sale deed in his favour.
It is also contended that when the defendant No.1 has issued notice to the defendant No.2 and asked for explanation, he never appeared.
The defendant No.1 has sought for dismissal of the suit against it.

4. The defendant No.2 filed a written statement wherein while admitting the grant of the original Site in favour of his father, he has denied the execution of the sale deed by his father in respect of Jayaram G vs The Karnataka Govt Empl Housing Society ... on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54298016/

sentences.text: It is also stated that Abdul Hafeez died in the year 1974 and after the death of Abdul Hafeez, the defendant No.2 being the legal heir was in possession of the property and the alternative Site No.102 came to be allotted in his favour and accordingly the sale deed was also executed on payment of 5,084/-.

It is his contention that he is in possession of the property pursuant to the grant and as there was no sale deed in favour of the plaintiff, question of allotment of alternative Site in favour of the plaintiff did not arise.

5. In the additional written statement filed by defendant No.2, he has taken up a contention that one G. Jayaram son of Gundappa is impersonated by the plaintiff Jayaram as he has not produced the original sale deed dated 29.09.1966 and lease deed of the year 1967.

It is also contended that the age of the plaintiff Jayaram is shown as 35 years and such being the case, he would have born only either in the year 1970 or 1971 and therefore the suit is filed by suppressing the real facts.

It is also contended that the plaintiff No.2 is not a bonafide purchaser as the Site No.341 was not in existence at the time of alleged agreement, said to be executed in favour of plaintiff No.2 and he is the trespasser over the suit schedule property.
It is also contended that the plaintiff No.2 has interfered with the possession of the defendant No.2 and therefore he has filed O.S.No.2191/2006.

It is further contended that defendant No.2 has executed a gift deed dated 02.03.2005 in favour of his wife Mumtazunnissa, who is now defendant No.2(a) and the plaintiff after keeping quiet from the year 1974 to 2004 almost for a period of 30 years now come up before this court and therefore the suit is barred by limitation.
In the written statement filed by the LRs of defendant No.2 after the death of defendant No.2 also, they have reiterated the same contentions.
On these contentions, they have sought for dismissal of the suit.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings this Court has framed the following issues and additional issues:-
ISSUES 1) Whether plaintiff proves that defendant No.1 has no right to re-allot the suit site in favour of 2nd defendant as pleaded in plaint para 9?
2) Whether plaintiff proves that sale deed dated 16.07.2003 in favour of 2nd defendant is null and void ab-initio?
3) Whether 2nd defendant proves that reallotment of suit site in his favour by City Improvement Trust Board is legal and valid?
4) Whether 1st defendant proves that 2nd defendant has fraudulently obtained sale deed from it as pleaded in para 7 of written statement?
5) Whether plaintiff is entitled for declaration for suit property as sought?
6) Whether plaintiff is entitled for mandatory injunction against defendant No.1 as sought?

REASONS 10. Addl. Issue No.5:-

It is an admitted fact that the suit schedule property was initially allotted to late Abdul Hafeez, who is the father of defendant No.2 and a registered sale deed was executed by defendant No.1 in favour of late Abdul Hafeez on 15.09.1962.

The contention of the plaintiffs is that after acquiring title, interest and possession over the suit schedule site, Abdul Hafeez has executed a registered sale deed in favour of the plaintiff on 29.09.1966 for a consideration amount of 1,500/-
and thereafter the plaintiff No.1 became the owner of the suit schedule property.
The LRs of defendant No.2 have seriously disputed the execution of the sale deed by late Abdul Hafeez in favour of the deceased first plaintiff No.1 G.Jayaram.

sentences.text: In support of the case of the plaintiffs in order to establish this contention, they have produced the original sale deed executed by defendant No.1 in favour of Abdul Hafeez on 15.09.1962, which is marked as Ex.P1.
Ex.P5 is the original registered sale deed executed by Abdul Hafeez in favour of deceased plaintiff G.Jayaram.
Ex.P.2 is the encumbrance register extract, which shows the transaction of the sale deed dated 29.09.1966 executed in favour of the deceased plaintiff Jayaram.
Further, the plaintiffs have also produced a certified copy of the registered lease deed dated 18.01.1967 executed by deceased plaintiff Jayaram in favour of one Krishna Rao at Ex.P7.

This document substantiates that after the purchase of the property by the deceased plaintiff G.Jayaram from Abdul Hafeez, he has acted upon and exercised his right of ownership over the suit schedule property.
The execution of the registered lease deed in favour of K.N. Krishna Rao is also reflected in Ex.P3 encumbrance certificate.
12. One of the contention raised by the contesting defendants is that the plaintiff G.Jayaram was impersonated as he was shown as aged 35 years at the time of filing of this suit in the year 2005.
But, subsequently, the plaint was amended.
The plaintiffs have also produced the death certificate of deceased plaintiff and other medical records to establish his identity.

Added to this custody of the original sale deed executed in favour of Abdul Hafeez by defendant No.1 and production of the original sale deed executed by Abdul Hafeez in favour of plaintiff G.Jayaram are the proof to show that plaintiff G.Jayaram is the person who has purchased the property from Abdul Hafeez for a valuable consideration.
It is brought on record that Abdul Hafeez died in the year 1974.
He has not at all challenged the sale deed executed in favour of the plaintiff No.1 G.Jayaram during his life time.

Therefore, the documents on record are sufficient to establish that late Abdul Hafeez has sold the suit schedule property in favour of the plaintiff G.Jayaram and he was the owner of the suit schedule property.
Hence, Additional Issue No.5 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issues No.1 to 4:-

It is an admitted fact that after sale of the suit schedule Site No.341 in favour of Abdul Hafeez the then City Improvement Trust Board did not approve the layout in which the Site No.341 was formed and while approving the layout plan, CITB has reserved land for civic amenities including widening of the road and consequently, entire plan was disturbed and sites earlier demarcated were disrupted.
It is also an admitted fact that consequent upon this, earlier Site No.341 was utilised for the purpose of civic amenities and therefore the defendant No.1 has assured to allot alternative Site.

It is also not in dispute that consequent thereupon the defendant No.1 has executed a registered sale deed in respect of the present suit schedule Site No.102 in favour of defendant No.2 Abdul Rakeeb in the capacity of the legal heir of Abdul Hafeez, who is the original allottee.

The grievance of the plaintiffs is that when Abdul Hafeez had already sold the earlier Site No.341 and relinquished his title in favour of the deceased plaintiff G.Jayaram, the alternative Site should have been granted in favour of the plaintiff and not to the legal heirs of late Abdul Hafeez.
14. In the written statement filed by the defendants itself, they have admitted the fact that the present suit schedule Site was allotted as alternative site to the earlier site No.341.
It is not the contention of the defendants that the present suit schedule Site was allotted to defendant No.2 independently without reference to the earlier allotment.

The sale deed executed in favour of defendant No.2 itself clearly recites that as the earlier site No.341 was reshuffled and disappeared the sale deed is executed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of defendant No.2.

Therefore,

sentences.text: it is established that the allotment and execution of the sale deed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of defendant No.2 is as an alternative site for the loss of earlier Site No.341 and not independent or separate allotment.
15. Now the question for consideration is as to who was entitled for the allotment of alternative site.

As stated above, when the suit schedule Site was allotted as alternative site for the loss of original site, the person who has a right over earlier site No.341 is the person entitled for the allotment of new site.

While answering Addl. Issue No.5, this court has already came to the conclusion that though the father of defendant No.2 late Abdul Hafeez was the original allottee, he has transferred the allotted site No.341 in favour of the deceased plaintiff for valuable consideration and the deceased plaintiff has acted upon it.
Therefore, the deceased plaintiff was a subsequent transferee for value and he is the assignee.
Under these circumstances, the person who lost the site is plaintiff and not defendant No.2 or his father.
Alternative site will be granted as a compensation for the loss of earlier Site.
Late Abdul Hafeez, though was the original allottee, he has sold the site in favour of the deceased plaintiff for valuable consideration and received the consideration amount.
Hence, the person who has suffered by the reshuffling of the sites is the deceased plaintiff and not late Abdul Hafeez or defendant No.2.
In such circumstances, if the alternative site is allotted to the heirs of original allottee it would result in unjust enrichment to the heirs of original allottee.

16. It is also important to note that in the written statement filed by defendant No.1, it has categorically stated that the defendant No.2 has made false representation, suppressed material facts and fraudulently obtained the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 in his favour.

The stand taken by defendant No.1 also supports the contention of the plaintiff that the defendant No.2 without disclosing the sale of Site No.341 in favour of the deceased plaintiff has made representation by suppressing the true facts and obtained the sale deed dated 10.07.2003.
It is not the contention of the defendant No.2 or his legal heirs that the sale deed executed by late Abdul Hafeez was communicated to defendant No.1.

Therefore, the stand of defendant No.1 is that if the sale deed executed in favour of the deceased plaintiff was made known to defendant No.1, it would have executed the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the present suit schedule Site and not in favour of deceased defendant No.2.
17.

It is also relevant to note that earlier the defendant No.2 had instituted O.S.No.2191/2006 against the plaintiff No.1(a) &
(b) and also plaintiff No.2 for the relief of declaration of title over the suit schedule Site.

The said suit in O.S.No.2191/2006 is tried by this Court and in the considered judgement dated 14.11.2016,
this Court has dismissed the suit filed by defendant No.2 and defendant No.2(a) holding that they have failed to establish their title over the suit schedule property.
The said judgment is produced at Ex.P.25.

In the said judgement, this Court in para No.19 & 20 this Court has observed as hereunder:-
"19.

site No.341 was altered which was shown in Ex.D.9 and D.10.
Parties have admitted that site No.341 was utilized for formation of roads and other civic amenities.

The sale deed further indicates that because of alteration or modification of layout by the Society in the year 1976, the Society decided to allot site No.102 to the original member/allottee who purchased property under Ex.D.9 i.e. T. Abdul Hafiz.
Therefore, Society without noticing the sale of property under Ex.D.10 called the plaintiffs to produce records of heir-ship and consent of other heirs.

The plaintiffs more particularly the plaintiff No.1 not disclosed the sale of site No.341 by his father in favour of G. Jayaram at the time of furnishing the records to the Society for execution of the fresh sale deed.
Therefore, the Society again executed the sale deed at Ex.P.1 in favour of plaintiff No.1 under the impression that T. Abdul Hafiz lost his site No.341.
The entire recital of Ex.P.1 makes it clear that site No.102 was sold by the Society in lieu of site No.341 and not in addition to site No.341.
It is not the case of the plaintiffs that site No.102 has been independently allotted either to plaintiff No.1 or to his father in addition to site No.341.
It is also not the case of the plaintiffs that Society has allotted two sites to the father of plaintiff No.1.
Therefore, I hold that site No.102 is in substitution of site No.341 because of acquisition of site No.341.
The object of execution of sale deed at Ex.P.1 to the members of the family of T. Abdul Hafiz was to compensate loss incurred due to acquisition of site No.341.

If the Society had knowledge of sale deed at Ex.D.1, the Society would not be executed the sale deed in favour of plaintiff No.1 produced at Ex.P.1.
20.
Ex.D.14 is the representation given by G. Jayaram to the Society for allotment of another site due to acquisition of site No.341 which was purchased by him under Ex.D.10.
It appears that the Society has not given any reply to such notice.
The representation was given after execution of sale deed at Ex.P.1.
Therefore, G. Jayaram in order to enforce his right instituted O.S.No.6609/2005.
The proceedings of such suit, Ex.D.14 and the recitals at Ex.P.1 clearly indicate that absolute title in respect of site No.102 has not been transferred from Society to plaintiff No.1 under Ex.P.1.
The title passed under Ex.P.1 is imperfect without noticing the right of the G. Jayaram under Ex.D.10.
Therefore, no evidentiary value has to be attached to Ex.P.1 to confer any right, title and interest in favour of plaintiff No.1 in site No.102.
Thus, I hold that plaintiff No.1 has not acquired absolute title over the schedule property under Ex.P.1.
When the plaintiff No.1 has not acquired absolute title, there cannot be transfer of better title to the plaintiff No.2 under Ex.P.2.
Therefore, even the plaintiff No.2 not acquired absolute title over the schedule property on the basis of the gift deed.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 and Additional Issue No.2 and 6 are answered in the Affirmative and Additional Issue No.5 is answered in the Negative".

The finding recorded in the said suit was on the ground that late Abdul Hafeez though was an original allottee had sold the earlier Site No.341 in favour of the deceased plaintiff and therefore defendant No.2 had no right to get this alternative site.
This judgement operates as resjudicata in so far as defendant No.2 and defendant No.2(a).
It is true that defendant No.2(b) & (c) were not parties in the said suit.
But, they are claiming right over the suit schedule site through deceased defendant No.2 Abdul Rakeeb.
Therefore, it operates as resjudicata.

Even if it is considered that this judgement do not operate as resjudicata against defendant No.2(b)
& (c), the plaintiffs have able to establish that they are entitled for the allotment of the suit schedule site in their favour.

Hence, though the defendant No.1 has executed the sale deed in favour of the defendant No.2 on 10.07.2003, it is not a valid sale deed and it was executed in favour of defendant No.2 by defendant No.1 as the defendant No.2 had suppressed the sale of earlier site No.341 made by Abdul Hafeez in favour of deceased plaintiff No.1.

Since defendant No.2 has not revealed about the execution of the sale deed by his father in favour of the deceased plaintiff, the only inference that can be drawn is that it was executed by by the suppression of facts by defendant No.2 and it amounts to fraud.
Consequently, issue No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative and issue No.3 in the negative and issue No.4 in the affirmative.
19. Additional Issue No.2:-
One of the contention raised by the contesting defendants is that the suit is barred by limitation.

It is contended by them that though the earlier Site No.341 was utilised for the purpose of civic amenities in the year 1974 itself, the plaintiffs have kept quiet for a period of 30 years till the year 2004 and therefore the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation.

But, in the present case, as rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiffs, the cause of action arose when the defendant No.1 has executed the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 in favour of defendant No.2.
Needless to mention that no time limit was fixed for the purpose of allotment of alternative site.
The defendant No.1 has not committed any default in allotting the alternative site.
The only grievance of the plaintiffs is that the alternative site should have been allotted in favour of the plaintiff No.1 and not to defendant No.2.
When there was no time limit prescribed for allotment of the alternative site, the use of earlier site for civic amenities cannot be considered as a starting point of limitation.
Further, it is not the contention of the defendants that there was rival claims by the deceased plaintiff as well as by defendant No.2 right from the year 1974.

Therefore, the plaintiff was waiting for alternative site and the defendant No.1 instead of allotting it in his favour, allotted it in favour of defendant No.2 by executing the sale deed dated 10.07.2003.

In view of this, the period of limitation starts when the sale deed was executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No.2 on 10.07.2003 and not from the date when the earlier Site was utilised for civic amenities.

Consequently, this additional No.2 is answered in the negative holding that the suit is not barred by limitation.
20.
Additional Issue No.3:-
The LRs of defendant No.2 have taken up a contention that the cause of action does not survive against them.
But, the sale deed was executed in favour of defendant No.2.
Admittedly, the legal heirs who are brought in this suit are the legal heirs of defendant No.2.
They have put forward a claim over the suit site by filing earlier suit.
Therefore, when the Lrs of defendant No.2 have claimed right over the suit schedule property, the right to sue survives against them.
Hence, addl. issue No.3 is answered in the negative.

sentences.text: 9 21. Additional Issue No.4:-
The defendants have taken up a contention that the suit claim is undervalued and insufficient court fee is paid.
The plaintiffs have valued the relief at Rs.5,084/- and paid court of Rs.128/-.
The defendant No.1 has executed the sale deed in favour of defendant No.2 for a consideration amount of 5,084/-.
Therefore, the value of the suit schedule property shall be considered as Rs.5,084/- on the date of filing of the suit.
Hence, the Court fee paid by the plaintiff is found sufficient.
Accordingly, Additional Issue No.4 is answered in the negative.
22. Issues No.5 to 7:-

In view of the answer given to the above issues, the defendant No.1 should have executed the sale deed in respect of the suit schedule site in favour of the deceased plaintiff G.Jayaram and not in favour of defendant No.2.

It is also brought on record that on 02.03.2005,
defendant No.2 has executed a gift deed in favour of defendant No.2(a).

When the allotment of the suit schedule site in favour of defendant No.2 itself is found invalid, the gift deed executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.2(a) dated 02.03.2005 also cannot convey any right, title or interest over the suit schedule property in her favour.
Therefore, the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 and gift deed dated 02.03.2005 are not binding on the plaintiffs' right to get the suit schedule site as alternative site.

In review of this, the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No.2 and gift deed dated 02.03.2005 executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.2(a) are declared as null and void and the defendant No.1 shall be directed to execute the sale deed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of the plaintiff.
Consequently, the issues No.5 & 6 are answered in the affirmative and the following order is passed:-
ORDER Suit is decreed with costs.
It is declared that the plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) are entitled for allotment of suit schedule Site in their favour.

The registered sale deed dated 10.07.2003 executed before the Sub Registrar,

The defendant No.1 is directed to execute a registered sale deed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of the plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) within 30 days from today.
The plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) shall bear all the expenses for the registration of the sale deed.
If the possession of the suit schedule site is with the defendants, they shall deliver it to the plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) on execution of the registered sale deed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is also not in dispute that consequent thereupon the defendant No.1 has executed a registered sale deed in respect of the present suit schedule Site No.102 in favour of defendant No.2 Abdul Rakeeb in the capacity of the legal heir of Abdul Hafeez, who is the original allottee.
The grievance of the plaintiffs is that when Abdul Hafeez had already sold the earlier Site No.341 and relinquished his title in favour of the deceased plaintiff G.Jayaram, the alternative Site should have been granted in favour of the plaintiff and not to the legal heirs of late Abdul Hafeez.
The sale deed executed in favour of defendant No.2 itself clearly recites that as the earlier site No.341 was reshuffled and disappeared the sale deed is executed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of defendant No.2.
Therefore,
Jayaram G vs The Karnataka Govt Empl Housing Society ... on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54298016/
6
it is established that the allotment and execution of the sale deed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of defendant No.2 is as an alternative site for the loss of earlier Site No.341 and not independent or separate allotment.
As stated above, when the suit schedule Site was allotted as alternative site for the loss of original site, the person who has a right over earlier site No.341 is the person entitled for the allotment of new site.
While answering Addl. Issue No.5, this court has already came to the conclusion that though the father of defendant No.2 late Abdul Hafeez was the original allottee, he has transferred the allotted site No.341 in favour of the deceased plaintiff for valuable consideration and the deceased plaintiff has acted upon it.
Therefore, the deceased plaintiff was a subsequent transferee for value and he is the assignee.
Under these circumstances, the person who lost the site is plaintiff and not defendant No.2 or his father.
Late Abdul Hafeez, though was the original allottee, he has sold the site in favour of the deceased plaintiff for valuable consideration and received the consideration amount.
Hence, the person who has suffered by the reshuffling of the sites is the deceased plaintiff and not late Abdul Hafeez or defendant No.2.
In such circumstances, if the alternative site is allotted to the heirs of original allottee it would result in unjust enrichment to the heirs of original allottee.
The entire recital of Ex.P.1 makes it clear that site No.102 was sold by the Society in lieu of site No.341 and not in addition to site No.341.
Even if it is considered that this judgement do not operate as resjudicata against defendant No.2(b)
& (c), the plaintiffs have able to establish that they are entitled for the allotment of the suit schedule site in their favour.
Hence, though the defendant No.1 has executed the sale deed in favour of the defendant No.2 on 10.07.2003, it is not a valid sale deed and it was executed in favour of defendant No.2 by defendant No.1 as the defendant No.2 had suppressed the sale of earlier site No.341 made by Abdul Hafeez in favour of deceased plaintiff No.1.
Since defendant No.2 has not revealed about the execution of the sale deed by his father in favour of the deceased plaintiff, the only inference that can be drawn is that it was executed by by the suppression of facts by defendant No.2 and it amounts to fraud.
But, in the present case, as rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiffs, the cause of action arose when the defendant No.1 has executed the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 in favour of defendant No.2.
The defendant No.1 has not committed any default in allotting the alternative site.
The only grievance of the plaintiffs is that the alternative site should have been allotted in favour of the plaintiff No.1 and not to defendant No.2.
When there was no time limit prescribed for allotment of the alternative site, the use of earlier site for civic amenities cannot be considered as a starting point of limitation.
Therefore, the plaintiff was waiting for alternative site and the defendant No.1 instead of allotting it in his favour, allotted it in favour of defendant No.2 by executing the sale deed dated 10.07.2003.
In view of this, the period of limitation starts when the sale deed was executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No.2 on 10.07.2003 and not from the date when the earlier Site was utilised for civic amenities.
Consequently, this additional No.2 is answered in the negative holding that the suit is not barred by limitation.
20.
Therefore, when the Lrs of defendant No.2 have claimed right over the suit schedule property, the right to sue survives against them.
When the allotment of the suit schedule site in favour of defendant No.2 itself is found invalid, the gift deed executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.2(a) dated 02.03.2005 also cannot convey any right, title or interest over the suit schedule property in her favour.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The plaintiffs have valued the relief at Rs.5,084/- and paid court of Rs.128/-.
The defendant No.1 has executed the sale deed in favour of defendant No.2 for a consideration amount of 5,084/-.
Therefore, the value of the suit schedule property shall be considered as Rs.5,084/- on the date of filing of the suit.
22. Issues No.5 to 7:-
Therefore, the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 and gift deed dated 02.03.2005 are not binding on the plaintiffs' right to get the suit schedule site as alternative site.
In review of this, the sale deed dated 10.07.2003 executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No.2 and gift deed dated 02.03.2005 executed by defendant No.2 in favour of defendant No.2(a) are declared as null and void and the defendant No.1 shall be directed to execute the sale deed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of the plaintiff.
Consequently, the issues No.5 & 6 are answered in the affirmative and the following order is passed:-
ORDER Suit is decreed with costs.
It is declared that the plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) are entitled for allotment of suit schedule Site in their favour.
The registered sale deed dated 10.07.2003 executed before the Sub Registrar,
Rajajinagar by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No.2 through document No.RJN-1-02467/2003-04 IN cd No.RJND3 of Book-1 (Non Testamentory Documents) and the gift deed dated 02.03.2005 executed by defendant No.2 in a defendant No.2(a) in document No.RJN-1-08051-2004-05, Book No.1, Stored in CD No.RJNND65 are declared as null and void.
The defendant No.1 is directed to execute a registered sale deed in respect of the suit schedule Site in favour of the plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) within 30 days from today.
The plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) shall bear all the expenses for the registration of the sale deed.
If the possession of the suit schedule site is with the defendants, they shall deliver it to the plaintiffs No.1(a) & (b) on execution of the registered sale deed.
Draw decree accordingly.
Registry shall forward the copy of the decree to the jurisdictional Sub Registrar to make necessary entries as required under Section 31(2) of the Specific Relief Act 1963.
